Tool call input: {'knowledge_bases': ['pubmed_papers'], 'search_rounds_budget': 5, 'search_target': "Find human clinical studies that measure serum interleukin-22 (IL-22) in early-stage Hashimoto thyroiditis (Hashimoto's thyroiditis) and directly compare with non-autoimmune thyroid disease and healthy controls. Determine whether serum IL-22 is increased, report numerical/group comparisons and the definition of early stage, and provide PubMed identifiers or source details."}

The relevant human study is **PMID 25079457**, “Serum interleukin-22 (IL-22) is increased in the early stage of Hashimoto's thyroiditis compared to non-autoimmune thyroid disease and healthy controls,” published in *Hormones* (Athens) in 2014.

Using a Quantikine ELISA, the study found serum IL-22 was higher in newly diagnosed, euthyroid, untreated Hashimoto thyroiditis (n=55; **42±34 pg/mL**) than in nodular-goiter patients without HT (n=30; **18±15 pg/mL**, P<0.001) and healthy controls (**20±13 pg/mL**, P=0.014). Nodular-goiter patients and healthy controls did not differ (P=0.496).

“Early stage” was characterized in the abstract as **newly diagnosed, euthyroid, untreated** HT; no time-from-onset threshold or further formal early-stage criteria were provided. The healthy-control sample size was not stated in the abstract.

The search found a direct human comparison with all three groups and statistically higher serum IL‑22 in newly diagnosed, untreated, euthyroid HT. I’ll check the evidence graph for an existing record before adding anything.

**Yes.** In a 2014 case-control study, serum IL‑22 was higher in newly diagnosed, euthyroid, untreated Hashimoto’s thyroiditis (55 patients; 42±34 pg/mL) than in nodular-goiter patients without HT (30 patients; 18±15 pg/mL; P<0.001) and healthy controls (20±13 pg/mL; P=0.014). Nodular-goiter and healthy-control levels did not differ significantly (P=0.496). The study’s “early stage” group was defined as newly diagnosed, euthyroid, and untreated; the abstract does not specify time since disease onset. **Source: PMID 25079457** (search evidence: `call_lhRMkYXo2fx7AcQjUOPn6IiB`, `call_6rhxQ1n94iew9Sa39XRuyx1t`).

FINAL DECISION: YES
